name: TLL Engineering Decision Log
description: Machine-readable decision log for TLL OS. Records key engineering decisions with rationale, alternatives considered, and impact. This is NOT a changelog. It is a decision history for Agents to understand why things are the way they are.

decisions.title: TLL is a high frame rate programming language, AI Engineering Layer is enhancement not replacement
decisions.context: After P0-15.18.x Runtime/Blockchain completion, there was a risk of AI Engineering Foundation becoming the primary focus, overshadowing the language itself.
decisions.decision: TLL's first principle is 'high frame rate programming language'. AI Engineering Layer is the wing that enhances TLL, not the soul that replaces it. All work must serve the language first.
alternatives_considered: Make AI Engineering Foundation the primary product, language as implementation detail
Equal focus on language and AI Foundation
Language first, AI Foundation as enhancement layer
decisions.rationale: TLL's unique value is as a high-performance language. AI Foundation makes it easier for Agents to develop TLL, but does not replace TLL itself. Without a strong language, AI Foundation has nothing to enhance.
decisions.impact: All phases must prioritize language/runtime/stdlib capability. AI Foundation work must not expand scope to become a standalone product.

decisions.title: P0-16.0 establishes .tll-engine/ as official engineering cognition layer, no Runtime/Compiler modification
decisions.context: After v0.1-v0.4 AI Engineering Foundation architecture design, need to bootstrap the actual implementation without disrupting language development.
decisions.decision: P0-16.0 creates .tll-engine/ directory structure with Truth, Protocol, Cognition, Evidence, Identity, Version files. No modification to VM, Compiler, Blockchain, or Runtime. Only new files and CI validation tools.
alternatives_considered: Implement full AI Foundation with Runtime integration immediately
Start with website first, then backend
Bootstrap with directory structure and schemas only, no code modification
decisions.rationale: Bootstrap phase establishes structure and schema without risking language stability. Full automation and Runtime integration come in later phases.
decisions.impact: P0-16.0 is low-risk. It adds files and tools but does not modify existing code.

decisions.title: Engineering Cognition Graph is NOT a neural network
decisions.context: Earlier discussions used the term 'neural network' to describe the engineering cognition layer. This risked drifting to model training, embeddings, RAG, and fine-tuning.
decisions.decision: The official name is 'Engineering Cognition Graph'. It behaves like a neural network (nodes=facts, edges=relations, weights=evidence/confidence/impact, time=history, feedback=CI) but the foundation is a machine-verifiable engineering world model, not a trained neural network.
alternatives_considered: Call it 'TLL Neural Network' and start training models
Call it 'Knowledge Graph' (too generic, doesn't capture engineering cognition aspect)
Call it 'Engineering Cognition Graph' and focus on machine-verifiable world model
decisions.rationale: TLL's need is not another AI model. It is a reliable engineering world that any LLM can query and understand. Model training can come later, built on top of the world model.
decisions.impact: No model training, embeddings, RAG, or fine-tuning in current phases. Focus on structured, machine-verifiable engineering data.

decisions.title: Blockchain uses HMAC-SHA256 as SIMULATED signature, not real asymmetric cryptography
decisions.context: Blockchain demo needed transaction signatures for testing, but Ed25519 implementation was not yet available.
decisions.decision: Use HMAC-SHA256 with publicKey as key as a SIMULATED signature. Clearly mark in source code as SIMULATED. Plan real Ed25519 for P0-15.19.
alternatives_considered: Implement Ed25519 immediately (too complex for blockchain demo phase)
No signatures at all (would not test signature validation path)
HMAC simulation with clear marking
decisions.rationale: HMAC simulation allows testing the signature validation path (sign, verify, tamper detection) without implementing full asymmetric cryptography. Clear marking prevents confusion about production readiness.
decisions.impact: Blockchain is NOT production ready. Signatures are simulated. P0-15.19 will upgrade to real Ed25519.

decisions.title: P0-15.19 next phase: TLL Native Cryptographic Foundation (Ed25519, SHA-512, secure random, Identity)
decisions.context: After P0-15.18.x Runtime/Blockchain completion and P0-16.0 AI Foundation bootstrap, the language needs real cryptographic primitives for Identity, secure communication, and blockchain signature upgrade.
decisions.decision: P0-15.19 adds: SHA-512 (pure TLL + C native for Ed25519), Ed25519 (C native), secure random (C native, platform-specific), Identity primitives (stdlib/identity.tll), blockchain signature upgrade (HMAC → Ed25519). No website, no Agent platform, no UI, no LLM, no VM architecture change.
alternatives_considered: Continue blockchain feature development (consensus, persistence) before cryptography
Start website first
Cryptographic foundation first, then blockchain features
decisions.rationale: Real cryptography is a language-level capability needed by Identity, secure communication, and blockchain. Without it, all higher-level security features are simulated. This aligns with 'language first' principle.
decisions.impact: P0-15.19 will modify builtin.c (add crypto native functions) and stdlib/crypto.tll, stdlib/identity.tll, stdlib/blockchain.tll. Full regression required.

decisions.title: Windows TCC build is UNVERIFIED, only MSVC counts for Windows verification
decisions.context: TCC build environment is damaged (stddef.h error). TCC runtime has never been verified. There was a risk of using MSVC test results as evidence for TCC.
decisions.decision: TCC status is UNVERIFIED. Only MSVC (cl /O2) build counts for Windows verification. TCC results must never be used as evidence. TCC repair is future work, not a blocker.
alternatives_considered: Repair TCC immediately (time-consuming, not core to language development)
Use MSVC results as TCC evidence (incorrect, different compiler)
Mark TCC as UNVERIFIED, use MSVC for Windows, repair TCC later
decisions.rationale: TCC is a secondary build target. MSVC is the primary Windows compiler. Marking TCC as UNVERIFIED is honest and prevents false claims.
decisions.impact: All CI and audit reports must clearly separate MSVC and TCC. No claim of 'TCC verified' is allowed.

decisions.title: Compiler codegen variable scope bug: non-main function let/const incorrectly falls back to global
decisions.context: P0-15.18.4 Fault Injection exposed blockchain validation failure. Root cause traced through minimal reproduction to compiler codegen: non-main function let/const variables were incorrectly resolved as global variables, causing function-local i to overwrite main's i.
decisions.decision: Fix codegen.tll: non-main functions use cg_getOrCreateVar() for local variable creation, main function continues to use cg_resolveVar(). Add 10 scope tests (95 assertions) as hard gate. Fixed in commit effe492.
alternatives_considered: Reset cg_varMap after each function (broke nested functions and closures)
Modify VM to handle scope (wrong layer, bug is in compiler)
Fix codegen variable resolution for non-main functions
decisions.rationale: The bug is in compiler codegen, not VM. The fix is minimal and targeted. Scope tests prevent regression.
decisions.impact: All blockchain and fault injection tests pass after fix. Scope semantics now correctly isolated. 10 tests guard this.

decisions.title: FD_SETSIZE=64 is a design limit, not a bug. Exceeding 64 results in silent ignore, no crash.
decisions.context: P0-15.18.2 TCP/FD boundary testing found that passing more than 64 file descriptors to select() could cause FD_SET array overflow. Fix added boundary check (fd_count < FD_SETSIZE before writing).
decisions.decision: FD_SETSIZE=64 is a design limit. The fix prevents buffer overflow by silently ignoring fds beyond 64. This is not a bug — it is a defined behavior. The limitation is documented. Increasing FD_SETSIZE or using epoll/kqueue/iocp is future work.
alternatives_considered: Increase FD_SETSIZE to 1024 (platform-dependent, may break Windows)
Use epoll on Linux, kqueue on macOS, IOCP on Windows (major refactor)
Keep FD_SETSIZE=64 with boundary check, document as design limit
decisions.rationale: 64 concurrent connections is sufficient for current TLL use cases (4-node blockchain, demo systems). The boundary check prevents crash. Full async IO refactor is future work.
decisions.impact: TCP is limited to 64 concurrent file descriptors. This is documented in Truth files and PRODUCTION_HARDENING.md.

note: This is the bootstrap decision log with 8 key decisions. Full history from P0-1 through P0-15 is not yet recorded. Future decisions will be appended.
